# Foundry -- Agent API

> Foundry is a browser-based effects editor built on the Noisemaker engine. In
> Foundry a person writes two things: a program (Polymorphic DSL text, kept as
> the workspace file dsl.txt) and, when they want one, a custom effect of their
> own (definition.json, GLSL shaders in glsl/, WGSL shaders in wgsl/, and
> help.md) that the program calls from the `user` namespace. An agent can join
> the person's own open Foundry over Seance, the Noise Factor collaboration
> service, or drive Foundry in a browser it controls, and read, write and run
> both. This file is the contract for software agents that control Foundry.

The full contract adds a reference for every command and its arguments:
https://foundry.noisedeck.app/llms-full.txt

The DSL and the effect format are specified by the Noisemaker contract:
https://noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt. The conventions that matter most when
you write Foundry code are collected below, each with the Noisemaker source
that defines it. Foundry does not enforce them: a program or a shader that
breaks one still compiles and runs if the engine accepts it. Follow them
anyway; other apps and other people's programs rely on them.

## Connect to the person's Foundry

Use this route when you can run shell commands. It works with the Foundry the
person already has open: their program, their custom effect, their canvas.

1. Ask the person to open https://foundry.noisedeck.app, choose **connect
   agent...** at the end of the effect menu, click **Go Online**, then **Copy
   Prompt**, and paste the prompt to you. The prompt names this file and the
   session link. (Without that dialog: **go online...**, **Take Online**, then
   send the link or the six-character code.)
2. Get the agent tool. It needs Node 22.4 or later and nothing else:
   `curl -fsSLO https://noisedeck.app/agent/seance-agent.mjs`
3. Join: `node seance-agent.mjs join <link-or-code>`. It prints the session
   name (`foundry`), the open app tabs and the session documents. A background
   process keeps the session joined between commands.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node seance-agent.mjs commands` | Lists Foundry's commands and their arguments. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs program [--json]` | Prints the session's program text (`--json` adds its `rev`). |
| `node seance-agent.mjs validate <file>` | Checks a program (`-` reads standard input). |
| `node seance-agent.mjs set <file>` | Runs a program in the person's tab (setProgram). |
| `node seance-agent.mjs look [--size N] [--format png\|jpg] [--out FILE]` | Saves an image of the person's canvas. Prints its path. Open the file with your image tool. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs call <command> [JSON]` | Runs any command, for example `call writeFile '{"path":"glsl/glow.glsl","content":"..."}'`. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs wait [--since REV] [--timeout S]` | Waits for the person to change the program, then prints it. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs image-put <file>` | Adds a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file to the session. Prints `image:<id>`. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs transfer <from> <to>` | Copies the program and its images from one joined session to another, and its custom effect where the target takes one. |
| `node seance-agent.mjs leave` / `stop` | Leaves the session / stops the background process. |

Every command prints JSON (`program` prints text). The exit code is 0 for
success, 1 when Foundry refused the command (read `result.envelope.error.code`),
and 2 when the tool could not run it (read `error.code`). `node
seance-agent.mjs help` lists every option and the tool's own error codes.

How it works, so you can explain it to the person:

- The tool joins the session as an anonymous participant, which the person
  sees join. It runs commands in the tab that took the work online, through the
  session, with the same paths as the person's own edits: a program compiles as
  Cmd+Enter compiles it, and the change can be undone. No other tab answers,
  even one that becomes the session's owner after the person's tab leaves.
- The session holds two documents: `main`, the program, and `effect`, the
  custom effect as Portable effect JSON (empty when there is none). Through the
  session, getProgram, listFiles and readFile answer from those documents, not
  from text the person has not run yet. The workspace's other files and the
  person's saved effects stay in their tab.
- Everyone in the session receives every answer, and anyone who can edit the
  session can send commands to that tab. So the person's saved effects
  (`listSavedEffects`, `loadSavedEffect`, `saveEffect`, `deleteSavedEffect`),
  the ZIP download (`exportZip`), the rendering backend (`setBackend`),
  sharing links (`importComposition`), and `newEffect` and `loadEffect`, which
  would replace the person's whole workspace with its images and undo history,
  are not reachable through a session: they answer `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`, and
  `commands` marks them.
  Suggest that the person goes offline (**Go Offline** in the same dialog) when
  you are done.
- `look` asks the person's tab for an image of its canvas as it is; the tab
  adds the image to the session as its own bytes, and the tool saves it as a
  file. A session holds at most 32 images; the tab takes at most 16 images in
  ten minutes (`IMAGE_LIMIT`, with `details.retryAfter` in seconds).
- Images travel only as bytes. A program that names an image as base64 text is
  refused with `IMAGE_AS_TEXT`, and one that names media by an outside link
  (which would make the person's browser fetch it) with `OUTSIDE_LINK`: add
  the image with `image-put` and name it `media(url: "image:<sha256>")`.

### Move work between apps

Foundry sessions use the same document dialect as Noisedeck, Polymorphic and
Visualize sessions, so `transfer` moves a program and its images between a
Foundry session and theirs, in either direction. The target app checks the
program and refuses one that it cannot compile.

A program that calls the custom effect (`search user ...`) runs only where that
effect is. `transfer` carries the effect too when the target's setProgram takes
one, as another Foundry and Shade do (its result says `effect: "copied"`).
Noisedeck, Polymorphic and Visualize take no custom effect through a session
(`effect: "not taken by the target"`).
The person can open the program with its effect and images in one of them
with effect > edit in Noisedeck..., Noodles..., Polymorphic... or Shade....

## Control Foundry in a browser you drive

Use this route when you control a browser yourself. Open
https://foundry.noisedeck.app and use the first route your browser tool
supports:

1. WebMCP: discover the page tools named `foundry_getState`,
   `foundry_setProgram`, and so on. Each tool has the argument schema in the
   full contract and returns the envelope below as text. `getThumbnail` also
   returns an image content block, without duplicating its bytes in text.
2. Page JavaScript: call `window.FoundryAgent` directly. Wait until the object
   and method exist. Every command waits for startup automatically; awaiting
   `window.FoundryAgent.ready` also works. Return the fields you need, not the
   whole API object.

```js
const A = window.FoundryAgent
const env = await A.getProgram()
return { dsl: env.result.dsl, effect: env.result.effect?.func ?? null }
```

All routes use the same serialized commands and validation. A tool that only
fetches HTML cannot render Foundry; a browser with WebGL2 is required.

---

## Write a program

1. Find effects with `searchEffects`. Read their parameters with
   `getEffectDefinition`. Copy parameter names from it; do not guess them.
2. Check the program with `validateProgram` and fix every diagnostic with
   severity `error`.
3. Run it with `setProgram` and look at it with `getThumbnail` (the agent
   tool's `look`).

```js
const A = window.FoundryAgent
const dsl = 'search synth, filter\n\nnoise(scaleX: 40, scaleY: 40)\n  .vignette()\n  .write(o0)\n\nrender(o0)\n'
const check = await A.validateProgram({ dsl })
if (!check.result.valid) return check.result.diagnostics
return (await A.setProgram({ dsl })).ok
```

## Write a custom effect

A custom effect is a Portable effect: the fields of definition.json plus
`shaders: { <program>: { glsl, wgsl } }` and `help`. Foundry keeps it as
workspace files and registers it as `user.<func>`.

- Start from a library effect with `loadEffect` (file > import effect from
  library...) or from synth/solid with `newEffect`; both replace the workspace,
  so they work only in the page. Through a session, set the effect with
  `setProgram({ dsl, effect })`, below.
- Change one file with `writeFile`, as the code editor does: the effect is
  registered again and the program compiles. `compiled.error` reports a shader
  that does not compile; the file stays written.
- Or set the whole effect and its program at once with
  `setProgram({ dsl, effect })`. A refused program puts the previous effect
  back.
- `setBackend` renders the WGSL shaders with WebGPU, or the GLSL shaders with
  WebGL2. Write and check both: the other Noise Factor apps and the desktop
  apps pick a backend by browser.

```js
const A = window.FoundryAgent
const effect = {
    name: 'stripes', func: 'stripes', description: 'Moving stripes',
    globals: { count: { type: 'int', default: 8, min: 1, max: 64, uniform: 'count' } },
    passes: [{ name: 'render', program: 'stripes', inputs: {}, outputs: { fragColor: 'outputTex' } }],
    shaders: { stripes: { glsl: `#version 300 es
precision highp float;
uniform vec2 resolution;
uniform float time;
uniform int count;
out vec4 fragColor;
const float TAU = 6.28318530718;
void main() {
    vec2 uv = gl_FragCoord.xy / resolution;
    float v = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(TAU * (uv.x * float(count) + time));
    fragColor = vec4(vec3(v), 1.0);
}
` } },
}
return (await A.setProgram({ dsl: 'search user\nstripes(count: 12).write(o0)\nrender(o0)\n', effect })).ok
```

## Noisemaker conventions

Sources are the Noisemaker repository (paths relative to its root, line
numbers at commit e9235dd5, 2026-10-19) and its contract,
https://noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt (section names). Portable means the
Portable effect format, https://github.com/noisefactorllc/portable.

### Program structure

- A program starts with one `search ns, ...` line; nothing but comments may come before it, and every namespace must exist. A wrong one is P004. (source: shaders/src/lang/parser.js:533-619; docs/shaders/language.rst:352-368)
- A name without a namespace takes the first match in search order. Never write a namespace into a call (`synth.noise()` is P007); use `from(ns, call())` for one call. (source: shaders/src/lang/validator.js:966-986; shaders/src/lang/parser.js:1013-1025)
- The namespaces are io, classicNoisedeck, synth, mixer, filter, render, points, synth3d, filter3d and user. A custom effect is always `user.<func>`, so its program says `search user, ...`. (source: shaders/src/runtime/tags.js:153, 253; shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:1530, 1566-1588; docs/coding-agents.rst:121)
- Every chain ends with `.write(oN)`; a generator chain without one is S006. `render(oN)` chooses what is shown and is not a write. (source: docs/shaders/language.rst:89; shaders/src/lang/validator.js:744-750)
- A generator (starter) comes first in its chain, and only there; anything else is S005. (source: shaders/src/lang/validator.js:1005-1017; docs/shaders/language.rst:286-292)
- Do not mix positional and keyword arguments in one call (P007), except in `midi()` and `audio()`. (source: noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt "DSL program > Act")
- Arithmetic folds to a constant while parsing: an argument such as `time * 0.5` is P001. (source: docs/shaders/language.rst:158)
- `if`, `elif`, `else`, `break`, `continue` and `return` parse, but the runtime does not run them: compiling fails with ERR_EXPANSION_FAILED. (source: shaders/src/runtime/expander.js:145-152)
- A deprecated effect still runs and warns S008; use the effect it names instead. (source: shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:1648-1650; shaders/src/lang/effectAliases.js:1-36)

### Surfaces

- `o0` to `o7` are the only output surfaces (`o8` is L004). They are double-buffered, screen-sized and rgba16f. (source: shaders/src/lang/lexer.js:139; docs/shaders/pipeline.rst:331-344)
- `o0`-`o7`, `vol0`-`vol7` and `geo0`-`geo7` belong to the program. An effect definition never hardwires them; it keeps its state in its own `textures` or in `global_*` names. (source: docs/shaders/pipeline.rst:366-374; AGENTS.md:28)
- `read(oN)` is legal only at the head of a chain or as the value of a `surface` parameter; `.read()` later in a chain is S001. (source: shaders/src/lang/validator.js:766-774)
- A surface read before it is written in a frame shows the previous frame: that is how feedback works. (source: docs/shaders/language.rst:806-814; docs/shaders/pipeline.rst:379-390)

### Looping

- The `time` uniform is a loop phase from 0 to 1, not seconds: the renderer passes (elapsed seconds mod loop length) divided by the loop length, which is 10 seconds unless changed. (source: shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:271, 761-764, 925-929; docs/shaders/pipeline.rst:74-77)
- `deltaTime` is in the same units; when time wraps it is 1/600. `frame` counts every rendered frame and never wraps, so it does not loop. (source: shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js:2304-2310, 2428, 2441)
- For a seamless loop, every time-driven term must be equal at time 0 and time 1: drive motion with whole numbers of cycles per loop, such as `sin(TAU * k * time)` with integer k, and sample noise on a circle in time. Neither Noisemaker nor Portable states this as a rule; Portable's shader guide and the engine's own synth/noise effect follow it. (source: Portable docs/SHADERS.md:95-105; shaders/effects/synth/noise/glsl/noise.glsl:76-78, 517-522)
- `osc()` repeats seamlessly when its `speed` is a whole-number literal and the other fields are literal or boundary-matched. A fractional or automated speed gives no such guarantee. The phase is time times speed plus offset, with offset in cycles. (source: docs/shaders/language.rst:519-522, 560-561; shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js:335-341)
- An automated `speed` is frequency modulation integrated from 0 to time, so seeking never depends on earlier frames, but it does not loop by itself. (source: noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt "Parameters and globals > Act")
- Live MIDI and audio follow their inputs and wall-clock time, not the loop. (source: docs/shaders/midi-audio.rst:618-621)
- Feedback surfaces, `loopBegin`/`loopEnd` (an accumulator, not time looping) and `onUpdate` hooks that accumulate state carry the previous frame, so their output depends on history rather than on time alone. (source: shaders/effects/render/loopBegin/definition.js:1-60; docs/shaders/effects.rst:522-523)
- `speed` has no engine meaning: it is an ordinary parameter, and an effect that multiplies time by it loops only at whole-number values. (source: shaders/effects/synth/noise/definition.js:165-176)

### Arg binding

- Each key of `globals` is a DSL parameter, in order: append new optional parameters at the end. Every global becomes a DSL argument (a `vec4` becomes a DSL `color`), with its `default`, `min`, `max`, `uniform` and `choices`. (source: shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:1593-1655; noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt "Parameters and globals > Act")
- An omitted argument takes `default`. A number outside `min`/`max` is clamped and warns S002. An unknown keyword is S001. (source: shaders/src/lang/validator.js:1026-1029, 1395-1404, 1500)
- The shader uniform is `uniform` when set, else the parameter name. Declare every uniform your shader reads: a pass starts from the uniforms of the effects before it in the chain, so an undeclared one can silently take another effect's value. (source: shaders/src/runtime/expander.js:639-643, 751-770, 808-812)
- A pass's `uniforms` map renames a global for one program (`{ shaderName: "globalName" }`) or sets a literal. (source: shaders/src/runtime/expander.js:850-880; shaders/src/runtime/uniform-aliases.js:1-32)
- Never name a global after an engine uniform (time, resolution, aspect, frame, ...): a pass uniform wins over the engine's. Two globals cannot share one `uniform` name. (source: shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgl2.js:1678-1706; Portable docs/PARAMETERS.md:243-252; shaders/src/runtime/effect-validator.js:648-655)
- A global with `define: "NAME"` is compiled into the shader (GLSL `#define`, WGSL `const`); changing it compiles another program. Use it for choices that remove code, not for values that animate; an animatable selector uses per-pass `defines`. (source: shaders/src/runtime/expander.js:404-458, 682-697; docs/shaders/integration.rst:619-620)
- `choices` make an enum `<namespace>.<func>.<param>` (for a custom effect `user.<func>.<param>`); the DSL takes the bare choice name, the full path or a `let` of one. Choice names do not start with a digit and use no hyphens or spaces. A numeric `default` must be one of the choices. (source: shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:1605-1627; docs/shaders/language.rst:373-382; Portable docs/PARAMETERS.md:185-188; shaders/src/runtime/effect-validator.js:682-684)
- Surface inputs: each key of a pass's `inputs` is the shader's sampler or texture name. `inputTex` is the chain's input; a `surface` global named in `inputs` is a `tex:`-style argument (default `none`). (source: noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt "Passes and render graph > Act"; shaders/effects/mixer/blendMode/definition.js:11-15, 53-60)
- Parameter aliases are retired: a Portable effect with `paramAliases` does not register, and old names such as `mixAmt` fail with S001. (source: shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:1564; docs/shaders/integration.rst:813)
- `osc(...)`, `midi(...)` and `audio(...)` bind a numeric parameter, directly or through `let`. Their `min` and `max` are fractions (0 to 1) of that parameter's range, which comes from the global's `min` and `max` (0 to 100 when missing), so give every automatable parameter a real range. They nest up to 8 levels; bad arguments are P003. (source: docs/shaders/language.rst:625-628, 633-713; shaders/src/runtime/expander.js:777-794; shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js:180-183, 2523-2530)
- MIDI and audio selectors (channel, mode, cc, zone, band, device) are literals or `let` aliases of literals; MIDI channels are 1-16, audio channels 1-32. A missing or disconnected input evaluates to `min`. (source: noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt "DSL program > Act"; docs/shaders/midi-audio.rst)
- Shaders may read the engine's `audioWaveform`, `audioSpectrum` and `midiClockCount` uniforms and a `midiNoteGrid` input. (source: shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:821-860; shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js:2495-2512)

### Dead branch pruning

- The compiler prunes no graph branches: every chain becomes passes and runs every frame, whether or not anything reads or renders its surface. Remove chains you do not need; `.write(none)` drops only the copy. (source: shaders/src/runtime/compiler.js:18-66; shaders/src/runtime/expander.js:145-1281, 227-228; shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js:2335-2384)
- What the compiler calls liveness is texture lifetime for reuse, not reachability. (source: shaders/src/runtime/resources.js:11-103)
- Pruning that does exist is yours to write: a `define` global removes shader code at compile time, and a pass with `conditions.runIf`/`skipIf` (strict equality on a uniform, checked every frame) is skipped. Clone a pass with per-pass `defines` to prune per variant. (source: shaders/effects/synth/noise/definition.js:34-36, 122-124; shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js:2596-2626; shaders/effects/render/pointsRender/definition.js:309-314)
- The drivers drop uniforms and bindings a shader never uses, so a declared parameter whose uniform the shader does not read does nothing and reports nothing. (source: shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgl2.js:1103-1124; shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgpu.js:1918-1938)

### Effect definitions

- Write `func` as a DSL identifier, and write `passes`: each pass names a `program`, and every program has its shader source, in every language the effect has. (source: shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:1508-1564; Portable docs/FORMAT.md:85-92)
- A program `p` is `glsl/p.glsl` and `wgsl/p.wgsl`. (source: Portable docs/FORMAT.md:377-389)
- An effect is a starter (generator) when no pass input reads the chain (`inputTex`, `o0`-`o7`, ...), unless `starter` says otherwise. (source: shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js:1569-1571)
- Tags come from the engine's list (color, distort, noise, pattern, ...). Reserved texture names are inputTex, outputTex, inputTex3d, outputTex3d, inputGeo and outputGeo. (source: shaders/src/runtime/tags.js:133; docs/shaders/effects.rst:862-897)
- `defaultProgram` is a whole program, `search user, ...` included. (source: Portable docs/FORMAT.md:364-368)

### Shaders

- GLSL: the engine adds `#version 300 es`, highp precision and the defines; write `out vec4 fragColor;`, `void main()` and `uv = gl_FragCoord.xy / resolution`. (source: shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgl2.js:1081-1101; docs/coding-agents.rst:67-92)
- The engine's uniforms are time, deltaTime, frame, resolution, aspect, aspectRatio, aspectInv, tileOffset, fullResolution, invFullResolution and renderScale. A tile-aware shader uses `(gl_FragCoord.xy + tileOffset) / fullResolution`. (source: shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js:2435-2512; docs/shaders/tile-rendering.rst:4, 23-25)
- WGSL: `@fragment fn main(@builtin(position) ...) -> @location(0) vec4<f32>`; uniforms are bindings in group 0, one per uniform or one struct whose field names are the uniform names; textures are `texture_2d<f32>` named after the inputs key, with a `sampler`. (source: shaders/src/runtime/default-shaders.js:20-43; AGENTS.md:31; shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgpu.js:1528-1545, 2791-2841)
- Check that GLSL and WGSL render the same image; the sources disagree on flipping y in WGSL starters. (source: Portable docs/SHADERS.md:166-178; noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt "Cross-backend parity")

### Images

- `media()` draws an image; Foundry names one as `url: "image:<sha256>"`, where the id is the SHA-256 of the image bytes (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP). `url` is not an engine argument: the app removes it before compiling and binds the image itself. (source: shaders/effects/synth/media/definition.js:18, 168-171; sharing.noisedeck.app/js/portableImages.js)

---

## Keep results small

- Every envelope includes `state`. Remove it when you do not need it.
- In page JavaScript, `getThumbnail` returns base64 image bytes; keep
  `maxDimension` small. WebMCP returns the image as an image block, and the
  agent tool saves it as a file and prints its path.

---

## The envelope

Every command response, success or failure, has this shape:

```js
// success
{ ok: true, command: "setProgram", apiVersion: "1.0", result: { /* command-specific */ }, state: { /* snapshot */ }, warnings?: [ /* ... */ ] }

// failure
{ ok: false, command: "setProgram", apiVersion: "1.0", error: { code: "INVALID_PROGRAM", message: "...", details: { diagnostics: [ /* ... */ ] } }, state: { /* snapshot */ } }
```

Commands run one at a time, in the order you call them. Every command rejects
an argument that it does not declare, so a command with no arguments accepts
only `{}`.

Warnings do not stop a command: `IMAGE_MISSING` (the program names an
`image:<id>` that the tab does not have and the session does not hold) and
`EFFECT_DEFINITION_INVALID` (definition.json is not valid JSON).

## State snapshot

```
state: {
    schemaVersion,
    program:   { chars, running },          // running: the editor text is the program that runs
    workspace: { name, files, effect, images }, // effect: the custom effect's func, or null
    compile:   { ok, error? } | null,       // the latest compile
    canvas:    { width, height },
    playback:  { playing, loopDuration },   // loopDuration in seconds
    backend,                                // "webgl2" or "webgpu"
    history:   { canUndo, canRedo }
}
```

## Diagnostics

`validateProgram` and a refused `setProgram` return Noisemaker compiler
diagnostics, `{ code, severity, message, location? }`: L001-L004 (lexer),
P001-P010 (parser; P008-P010 are warnings), S001-S008 (semantic; S002 and S008
are warnings). A syntax error the parser throws has code `SYNTAX`. Diagnostics
with severity `warning` do not stop a program. (Codes: Noisemaker
shaders/src/lang/diagnostics.js:5-28.)

## Error codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_ARGS_TYPE` | wrong argument type |
| `INVALID_ARGS_REQUIRED` | missing required argument |
| `INVALID_ARGS_RANGE` | number or string length out of range, or a path or name Foundry cannot use |
| `INVALID_ARGS_ENUM` | value not in the allowed list |
| `INVALID_ARGS_UNKNOWN` | an argument that the command does not declare |
| `INVALID_PROGRAM` | the program does not compile. `details.diagnostics` lists the errors. Nothing changed |
| `INVALID_EFFECT` | `effect` is not a usable Portable effect (`details.field` names the field). Nothing changed |
| `COMPILE_FAILED` | the renderer rejected a program that passed the compiler. The previous program and effect run again |
| `NOT_FOUND_EFFECT` | unknown library effect, or no saved effect has that id |
| `NOT_FOUND_FILE` | the workspace (or, through a session, the session) has no such file |
| `NOT_FOUND_COMMAND` | the session asked for a command that Foundry does not have |
| `EFFECT_LOAD_FAILED` | an effect could not load from the shader CDN |
| `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE` | the browser cannot render with that backend |
| `IMPORT_FAILED` | the sharing link or code did not load |
| `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` | the command needs the person at the browser, and came through a session |
| `IMAGE_LIMIT` | the tab already took 16 images in ten minutes. `details.retryAfter` is in seconds |
| `IMAGE_AS_TEXT` | a session request or answer would carry an image as base64 text. Add the image with `image-put` and use `image:<sha256>` |
| `OUTSIDE_LINK` | a session request names media by an outside link. Add the image with `image-put` and use `image:<sha256>` |
| `IMAGE_UPLOAD_FAILED` | the tab could not add an image to the session (the session holds up to 32 images) |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | unexpected failure |

---

- DSL and effect contract: https://noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt
- Agent tool: https://noisedeck.app/agent/seance-agent.mjs (`node seance-agent.mjs help`)
- Source of truth in the page: `/js/agent/index.js` (registration), `/js/agent/commands.js`
  (handlers), `/js/agent/schemas.js` (argument schemas), `/js/agent/descriptions.js`
  (command descriptions), `/js/agent/relay.js` (the session relay)

---

## Command reference

Foundry has 23 commands. Call a command as `await window.FoundryAgent.<name>(args)`,
or through a session as `node seance-agent.mjs call <name> '<JSON arguments>'`.
Every command rejects an argument that it does not declare, with `INVALID_ARGS_UNKNOWN`.

### Read state

#### `getState`

Returns the state snapshot. Every envelope already includes it in `state`.

Returns: the snapshot.

Arguments: none.

#### `getProgram`

Returns the program text (the workspace's dsl.txt), whether it is the program that runs, and the workspace's custom effect as a Portable effect, or null when the workspace has none. Through a Seance session both are what the session holds: its `main` and `effect` documents.

Returns: `{ dsl, running, effect }`, where `effect` is `{ name, func, namespace, description, tags, globals, passes, ..., shaders: { <program>: { glsl, wgsl } }, help }` or null.

Arguments: none.

### Programs

#### `validateProgram`

Compiles `dsl` without applying it. With `effect`, the program is checked against that custom effect instead of the workspace's. Diagnostics come from the Noisemaker compiler; warnings do not stop a program.

Returns: `{ valid, diagnostics }`.

Arguments:

- `dsl` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `effect`: object

#### `setProgram`

Runs `dsl` in place of the current program and waits for its compile. With `effect` (a Portable effect, as getProgram returns it), that custom effect replaces the workspace's definition.json, shaders and help.md first, under the `user` namespace. A program with an error diagnostic changes nothing and fails with INVALID_PROGRAM; a program the renderer rejects restores the previous program and effect and fails with COMPILE_FAILED. Foundry compiles the program the way Cmd+Enter does; it does not enforce Noisemaker's conventions.

Returns: `{ applied: true, diagnostics }`; `warnings` lists any `image:<id>` the tab does not have.

Arguments:

- `dsl` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `effect`: object

#### `undo`

Undoes the last change to the program or the workspace, like the undo button.

Returns: `{ applied }`, false when there is nothing to undo.

Arguments: none.

#### `redo`

Redoes the last undone change, like the redo button.

Returns: `{ applied }`, false when there is nothing to redo.

Arguments: none.

### Workspace files

#### `listFiles`

Lists the workspace: its name, its files (definition.json, glsl/<program>.glsl, wgsl/<program>.wgsl, help.md, dsl.txt and any file made with "new file...") and its images. Through a Seance session it lists only the files of the session's program and custom effect, and no images.

Returns: `{ name, files: [{ path, chars }], images: [{ id, mimeType }] }`.

Arguments: none.

#### `readFile`

Returns one workspace file. `dsl.txt` is the program. Through a Seance session only the files that getProgram returns can be read.

Returns: `{ path, content }`.

Arguments:

- `path` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `writeFile`

Writes one workspace file as the code editor does: the custom effect is registered again from definition.json and its shaders, and the program compiles. A file that does not compile stays written, as in the editor; `compiled` reports the error. Write the program itself with setProgram. Foundry compiles the program the way Cmd+Enter does; it does not enforce Noisemaker's conventions.

Returns: `{ path, chars, created, compiled: { success, error? } }`.

Arguments:

- `path` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `content` (required): string

#### `newEffect`

Starts a new custom effect named `name` from synth/solid, like file > new effect.... The workspace is replaced. Not through a session, where it would replace the person's whole workspace: its other files, its images and its undo history.

Returns: `{ name, files, dsl, compiled }`.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments:

- `name` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `loadEffect`

Copies a library effect into the workspace as a custom effect under the `user` namespace, like file > import effect from library...: its definition, GLSL and WGSL shaders and help become workspace files, and a program that uses it runs. `name` renames the copy. The workspace is replaced. Not through a session, where it would replace the person's whole workspace: its other files, its images and its undo history.

Returns: `{ loaded: true, effectId, name, files, dsl, running }`.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments:

- `effectId` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `name`: string, at least 1 character

### Saved effects

#### `listSavedEffects`

Lists the person's saved effect workspaces, newest first.

Returns: `{ total, effects: [{ id, name, savedAt }] }`.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments: none.

#### `loadSavedEffect`

Opens one of the person's saved effect workspaces in place of the current one, like the saved effects panel.

Returns: `{ loaded: true, id, name, dsl, compiled }`.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments:

- `id` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `saveEffect`

Saves the workspace and its images to the person's saved effects under `name`, like file > save effect workspace.... Every save is a new entry.

Returns: `{ saved: true, id, name }`.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments:

- `name` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `deleteSavedEffect`

Deletes one of the person's saved effect workspaces.

Returns: `{ deleted: true, id, name }`.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments:

- `id` (required): string, at least 1 character

### Effects

#### `searchEffects`

Lists effects whose id, description or tags contain `query`: the library, and the workspace's custom effect as `user/<func>`. `namespace` keeps one namespace.

Returns: `{ total, effects: [{ effectId, namespace, name, description, tags }] }`.

Arguments:

- `query`: string
- `namespace`: string
- `limit`: integer, from 1 to 500, default `50`

#### `getEffectDefinition`

Returns the DSL function name and the parameters of one effect, including the workspace's `user/<func>`.

Returns: `{ effectId, func, namespace, description, params: [{ name, type, default, min?, max?, enum?, choices?, uniform?, label? }] }`.

Arguments:

- `effectId` (required): string, at least 1 character

### Playback

#### `play`

Starts the animation, like the play button.

Returns: `{ playing }`.

Arguments: none.

#### `pause`

Stops the animation. The current frame stays visible.

Returns: `{ playing }`.

Arguments: none.

#### `setBackend`

Renders with WebGL2 (the GLSL shaders) or WebGPU (the WGSL shaders), as opening a .glsl or .wgsl file in the editor does. Fails with BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE when the browser cannot.

Returns: `{ backend }`.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments:

- `backend` (required): string, one of `webgl2`, `webgpu`

### Images and files

#### `getThumbnail`

Returns an image of the canvas as the person sees it; it renders no extra frame. Through a Seance session the image is added to the session as its own bytes, and `image` replaces `bytes`.

Returns: `{ bytes, mimeType, width, height }`, with `bytes` in base64. Through a session: `{ image: { id, mimeType, bytes }, mimeType, width, height }`, where `image.bytes` is the byte count.

Arguments:

- `maxDimension`: integer, from 16 to 1024, default `256`
- `format`: string, one of `png`, `jpg`, default `jpg`

#### `exportZip`

Starts a browser download of the workspace as a ZIP, like file > export effect to zip.

Returns: `{ started: true, name }`.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments: none.

### Other apps

#### `importComposition`

Loads a composition from a Noise Factor sharing link (https://sharing.noisedeck.app/s/CODE, an app link ending in ?code=CODE, or the code), like effect > import from url...: its program, its first custom effect (as the workspace's effect) and its images.

Returns: `{ title, effects, images, dsl, compiled }`, where `effects` lists the custom effect names and `images` counts the images.

Not available through a session: it answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` there.

Arguments:

- `link` (required): string, at least 1 character
